title: HITL Request
description: A typed, transport-agnostic decision request emitted by the Orchestration Runtime (Component 4) at every Human-in-the-Loop gate (Component 5). It is the enriched form of the LangGraph interrupt payload: where the runtime once paused with only {artifact, turn}, it now emits a routable, renderable HITLRequest that any surface — stdin, a webhook, SMS, or a Discord channel — can present to the founder without knowing anything about the runtime internals. The founder's reply conforms to FounderResponse ($defs). Single source of truth shared between Ch.3 prose (§3.7 Orchestration Runtime, §3.8 HITL Contract) and prototype code.

request_id.description: Unique id for this gate instance. Correlates the rendered prompt (e.g. a Discord message) with the parked run so the founder's reply can resume the right interrupt. Distinct from thread_id: one run (thread_id) may raise many requests across its turns.

thread_id.description: The LangGraph run/flow identifier — the checkpointer resume key. The surface adapter passes this back unchanged so Crew.author_flow can resume the correct run, even after a process restart.

venture_id.description: Which venture raised this request (matches Venture Brief venture_id). Lets one deployment route requests from multiple ventures to distinct destinations.

turn.description: 1-indexed gate turn within the run. A surface can branch on first vs subsequent revisions (e.g. thread the second review under the first).

role.description: The role on whose behalf the founder is being asked to decide. Drives surface routing (which channel) and presentation (display name, avatar).

name.description: Role name as defined in the Role Library, e.g. 'marketing', 'customer_support', 'finance'.

display_name.description: Human-facing label for rendering, e.g. 'Marketing'. Defaults to a title-cased name if absent.

channel.description: Logical destination key the surface maps to a concrete channel — e.g. 'ads-report', 'customer-support', 'dev', 'finance'. Deliberately decoupled from any surface's native channel IDs: the runtime names an intent, the adapter owns the binding. Defaults to the role name if absent.

action.description: The action being gated — the entry from the role's DecisionRights.must_escalate that triggered this request, e.g. 'final_approval_before_publish', 'refund_request', 'deal_close'. Tells the founder what they are authorising, not merely that something needs review.

escalation_reason.description: Plain-language statement of why founder authority is required here, suitable for direct display. e.g. 'Marketing may draft and revise copy but must escalate before anything is published.'

artifact.description: The payload under review. Kept as an object (not a bare string) so surfaces can render a summary plus full content, and so non-text artefacts (a proposed refund amount, a price) fit the same envelope.

content.description: The full draft / proposal / payload text the founder reviews.

summary.description: One-line precis for notification surfaces (push notification body, channel preview) where the full content is too long.

options.description: The founder responses this gate accepts, in display order. Each maps to a FounderResponse.action value and gives the surface a label to render (a Discord button, an SMS keyword). Defaults to the canonical three (approve / reject / kill) if absent.

action.description: The decision token returned in FounderResponse.action.

label.description: Founder-facing button/keyword label, e.g. 'Approve & publish', 'Send back with notes', 'Kill run'.

requires_feedback.description: If true, the surface must collect free-text feedback before submitting this response (e.g. open a modal on 'reject').

context.description: Optional supporting material the surface may show on demand (a 'details' expander). None of it is required to render the decision.

prior_draft.description: The previous draft, on revision turns — lets the surface show a diff or before/after.

feedback_history.description: Founder feedback given on earlier turns of this run, oldest first.

task_description.description: The originating task, e.g. 'Draft a launch announcement for the Passly wallet pass'.

links.description: Relevant URLs (the trace, a preview, a dashboard).

estimated_cost_eur.description: Optional token/spend estimate for this run so far, for founder awareness.

urgency.description: Routing/notification hint. 'blocking' means the run is parked until the founder responds (the default for an author-flow gate); 'fyi' is a notification with no parked run behind it.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the runtime stamped when raising the request. Used for SLA display and ordering.

FounderResponse.title: Founder Response
FounderResponse.description: The founder's reply to a HITLRequest, produced by whatever surface rendered it. Maps one-to-one onto the FounderDecision dataclass in src/solo_founder_crew/hitl.py, plus the request_id needed to resume the correct parked run. The runtime ignores request_id once correlated and constructs FounderDecision(action, feedback).

request_id.description: Echoes the HITLRequest.request_id this responds to.

feedback.description: Free-text guidance. Present iff action == 'reject' (mirrors FounderDecision.feedback). The runtime feeds it to the revise step.

responder.description: Optional identity of who responded (the founder's handle on the surface). For audit; the single-founder unit of analysis makes this informational.

responded_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the response was submitted.
